answer: Admission is an auction on a fixed trellis: each identity must win one rung, and rung k reserves at 40 plus 3 times k minus 1, so price climbs with each slot. A winning bid carries a pigment marker bound to one key, never transferable, and each past win is kept as a relic, a public price record verifiers re-check. The 1,000th identity therefore pays 3,037, and 1,000 fakes pay 1,538,500 in total, while an honest agent wins one rung at 40. A bid-suppression ring fails because the reserve rises by rung regardless of collusion, and outsiders may take any rung at reserve.
